column2: A woodwind instrument that sounds rather like a duck having an existential crisis.
An ailment brought on by a student diet or the revenge of a dodgy late-night kebab.
The science proving that if your neighbour has eaten two chickens and you have had none, on average you are both quite full.
A contraption allowing one to feel like a fish without going to the bother of growing gills.
An ear infection caused when it wasn't an opera singer serenading your ear, but a nasty British draught.
The final boss at university, whose autograph you only seek right before being sent down.
A psychological term for someone whose ideal party is the one they didn't attend.
A swift, dangerous sea fish with a Hollywood smile and the manners of a back-alley hooligan.
A prickly sea creature that looks as though it were designed by committee for a horror film.
An ancient Egyptian who took the phrase 'tucking oneself in with a blanket' far too literally.
A sun-drenched island of beaches and dreadlocks, where nobody rushes anywhere thanks to Bob Marley.
The Irish poet who penned 'Those Evening Bells'.
A churchly aroma guaranteed to banish both demons and uninvited guests from the parlour.
A tiny bit of fire from which, according to the classics, a mighty blaze is kindled.
The substance that turns leaves green and makes vegetarians believe they are dining on sunshine.
The chap who made billions from a talking mouse in shorts scurrying across the cinema screen.
A massive island named 'green' purely to troll the very first Viking tourists.
Indigenous New Zealanders who politely poke their tongues out at opponents before a rugby match.
The place where one chews on the granite of knowledge with a terribly posh accent.
The Fab Four from Liverpool who had the entire world singing 'Yesterday'.
The Swedish capital that lent its name to the syndrome of falling for one's captors.
The largest and purest glass of fresh water on the planet.
A portable organ that, at a wedding, easily transforms into a weapon of mass merriment.
A musical genre under whose influence it is physically impossible to do anything in a hurry.
A pilot who flies so brilliantly that even the laws of physics look on with a nod of respect.
A horse that still cannot decide whether it is having a black-stripe or white-stripe sort of day.
An atmospheric layer that catches UV rays, radio waves, and meteors like a premier goalkeeper.
An underwater lift for those who find the ocean floor far more thrilling than a deckchair on the beach.
A mineral that stood in for window glass back when double glazing wasn't even a glint in a builder's eye.
A ship's elongated nose that always pokes into maritime business first (and holds the foresails).
A naval officer who is no longer a rating, yet still has a terribly long voyage ahead to become an admiral.
The blade a surgeon uses for a 'tiny incision' while you are fast asleep.
The magic ingredient that turns a simple broth into a proper savoury jelly or a bag of gummy bears.
A hard-working gas that freezes itself silly just so your pint in the fridge stays properly chilled.
A cosmic merry-go-round that astronauts find rather tricky to step off.
A gentle sea wind that caresses the face—right up until it decides to become a gale.
A muscular little vehicle that hauls away things other machines wouldn't dare budge.
The sound emitted by a river steamer or a thoroughly vexed driver stuck in traffic.
The centre of the Earth, an atom, an apple, or what Baron Munchausen used as a cannonball.
A St Petersburg palace where cats are officially on the payroll while humans wear their shoes out chasing beauty.
A place that, if you gaze into it long enough, politely gazes right back at you.
A vessel where elements transform, or the heart of a nuclear power station that is best not provoked.
Someone whose poster hangs above your bed and whose life you envy in the nicest possible way.
The world's smallest country, where the density of Popes per square mile is off the charts.
A sea cow that looks remarkably like a very kind, well-fed loaf of bread.
A creature made of water and wobble that delivers a rather painful kiss at the seaside.
A two-legged, eco-friendly cab where the driver doubles as the horsepower.
A marine delicacy that looks like an alien embryo, yet goes down a treat with a cold pint.
A bug that impersonates a twig with Oscar-worthy dedication whenever you look at it.
A geometric shape on which circus acrobats cheerfully risk their necks under the big top.
A large wild cat with a fondness for mountains and sportswear logos.
An ancient master of ceremonies who chatted with the gods without a middleman.
A battlefield for folks with rackets, where everyone grunts as though they were in the dentist's chair.
A nunchuck-wielding Ninja Turtle, or the chap who spent four years painting a ceiling flat on his back.
The main square in ancient Rome where everyone argued, or an internet site where everyone does the exact same thing.
A volcano's front door, or a dimple on the face of the Moon.
A chap who waves a stick non-stop and pretends to steer the orchestra, while the musicians pretend to understand him.
The sailing vanguard right at the bow, forever arguing with the jib over who gets to go first.
The staysail's trusty sidekick—another triangular sail perched on the ship's nose.
A high-altitude lake whose name makes schoolboys giggle in geography, while locals calmly build reed islands on it.
A French island with an Italian accent that gifted the world one notoriously ambitious, rather short emperor.
An Italian felt legend that turns any chap into Al Capone, Alain Delon, or a dapper screen gangster.
The iconic American headgear obliged to sit atop any self-respecting cowboy or sheriff in a Western.
